 China is developing a trimaran submarine that combines the concept of a semi-submersible missile carrier with an uncrewed platform.
 The vessel is undergoing tests in Huludao, in the Bohai Bay area. It was transported there from the southern city of Guangzhou via the port of Dalian, according to Naval News .
 The vessel is designed to carry a large number of missiles and launch them using targeting data from other ships, aircraft or satellites.
 The central hull houses two missile compartments containing launch canisters. The total number of missile launch cells is estimated at 16 to 18.
 To launch its weapons, the submarine must surface, open the compartment doors and raise the launchers into a vertical position.
 Image of the Chinese trimaran submarine. 2026. Illustration by H I Sutton 
 The vessel may carry anti-ship missiles or land-attack cruise missiles. Possible options include YJ-20 missiles, which are used on Type 055 destroyers.
 The hull design, with additional side floats at the stern, provides stability while underway and when stationary on the surface. These elements compensate for shifts in the center of gravity as the missile canisters are raised.
 The vessel is equipped with a snorkel to allow its diesel engines to operate while submerged. Its propulsion system consists of main propellers or waterjets for diesel-powered operation, along with electric propellers on the side floats.
 The trimaran has a submerged displacement of approximately 900 metric tons. The weapons compartment occupies most of the vessel’s internal space.
 YJ-20 missile launch. Photo: China Military Bugle 
 Due to the lack of available interior space, the vessel is believed to be uncrewed. The bridge at the top is intended only for control during port entry and maneuvering in roadsteads.
 Its operating concept resembles that of diesel-powered submarines from the Cold War era, which surfaced to launch missiles.
 Militarnyi previously reported that Russia had transferred technical documentation and materials to China for submarine testing.
